steps.name: Mechanist
steps.text: This smell is familiar...

steps.name: Mechanist
steps.text: Too bad there's still work to be done. I miss the sensation of alcohol rushing through my body.

options: I've heard your special drink is machine oil.
I've heard you stand on a chair and recite poems when you get drunk.

steps.name: Mechanist
steps.text: You're listening to Blaze, huh?

steps.name: Mechanist
steps.text: She's always complaining about all the rumors there are about her, and complaining that I take things too rough in her weapon test sessions.

steps.name: Mechanist
steps.text: 'Machine oil' is the name of my favorite cocktail.

steps.name: Mechanist
steps.text: Regular patrons of Just One More Pint know it well.

steps.name: Mechanist
steps.text: If you want to dig deep into those kinds of rumors, Doctor, take Blaze up on it next time she invites you to drink.

steps.name: Mechanist
steps.text: Logos and the others will—

steps.name: Mechanist
steps.text: Let's just say that what you see will make you forget any rumors about me.

steps.name: Mechanist
steps.text: Have you found your man, Saria?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: He spends twenty hours a day here.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Two Trimounts Sunshines, please.

steps.name: Mechanist
steps.text: You don't look like someone who drinks during work hours.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: I'm not.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: I've never been one to let alcohol interfere with my brain, regardless of the hour.

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: Live a little, Saria.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Both of these are yours.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: And you'd better pull yourself together, because I'm not buying a third.

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: What? Have you gone homeless too, after leaving Rhine?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: How many drinks I'm willing to buy for you depends on how much your information is worth to me.

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: Well then, spit it out. What do you want to know?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: See the liquid in this test tube?

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: Hm? Hmm...

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: It's not for drinking.

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: Well then, why are you asking me?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Show me your right hand.

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: What are you doing?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: You're right-handed, but you're holding the glass with your left.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Does your right arm still hurt from the subdermal Arts Unit implant?

steps.name: Mechanist
steps.text: The what?

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: Saria...

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: Who's the helmet, and the hood?

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: Rhine Engineering? Volvort Kochinski? Maybe... one of those places whose name we dare not speak?

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: Did they change their minds? Decide to shut me up forever?

steps.name: Mechanist
steps.text: I promise you, I have nothing to do with any of the organizations you mentioned. Not now, not ever.

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: Promise? Words like that ain't even worth the booze in front of me.

steps.name: Mechanist
steps.text: Doctor, he may not be willing to talk with us here.

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: It's you I don't trust, especially not that getup.

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: You reek of the Columbian tech elite, know what I mean?

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: The hood can stay. I feel better about you.

options: Why don't you take a break, Mechanist?
How about you go get yourself a drink?

steps.name: Mechanist
steps.text: Alright, I'll be over there.

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: Saria, you've picked up so many tabs for me, let me give you some honest advice.

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: Don't dig any deeper, if you don't want to end up like me.

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: This test tube of yours, that power armor—you're biting off more than you can chew.

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: Yes, more than even you can chew.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Do you understand what it is you've just said?

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Of course.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: It was you who reminded me. I'm not senile yet.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: This is a very serious accusation.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Is it now? An accusation?

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Oh, the accusation that you have something to do with Muelsyse's disappearance? Or the one that you're trying to seize control of Rhine Lab?

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: You need stronger evidence than that to blackmail me.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Relax, old friend.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: How long have we worked together? Ten years and then some?

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Did you think I was the type to come chat with an old friend carrying a bunch of papers, voice recordings and legal drafts?

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: You...

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Just because you did it to me doesn't mean I intend to return the favor.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Columbians like to put everything on the negotiating table. But you forget, I'm a cunning old Leithanian goat, who likes to play dumb.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: What exactly do you want?

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Just passing by, and to encourage an old friend.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: I don't understand. I thought you were on Control's side.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: You don't understand? We're researchers, after all. There's always more we don't understand than we do. That's part of the fun.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: You're a lot like Kristen. Too young, and too smart.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: You're always trying to fly high, not realizing how difficult it is for the others to keep up with you.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: All I want is to be left in peace to do my research, and not be dragged along the ground.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: It may only take a couple of years of your administration for the military and big capital to pick Rhine Lab to the bone, but it won't happen tomorrow.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: I'm surprised you have such a high opinion of me.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: You'll need to deal with the Director of Defense first, however, in order to get to Kristen.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: I didn't think Defense had a director.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Look at you, your memory failing at such a tender age.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Kristen never accepted Saria's resignation.

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: I never understood how you think, Saria.

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: No one talks about that ever since everything went down at Loken... my old employer.

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: They all chose to cut ties, no matter how much or how little they knew about the experiments.

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: That's what smart people do.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Does that mean you're not smart?

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: Ha... tongue still as sharp as ever, huh?

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: I would run if I could. They won't let me.

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: You ask if my right hand hurts? Of course it does! But did you think they would let me live this long if I didn't give up my hand and become a test subject?

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: I was the goddamned surgeon! Even if I had no idea what they wanted me to implant!

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Still capable of anger, I see. Looks like alcohol hasn't completely numbed you.

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: You've changed, Saria.

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: I could see you were angry when you first came to me, a few years ago.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: You weren't exactly wearing it on your face.

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: But I could see it. I felt the same way, when I learned what kind of experiments I was involved in.

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: There are other ways, if you want to take down Rhine Lab.

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: You're one of the founders. Anybody after Rhine will be queueing up to take your hand.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Taking down Rhine won't solve anything.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Kill one beast, only for its flesh and blood to feed yet more beasts. The fall of Loken Watertank is proof.

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: Excuses.

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: You've gone all over the place for Rhine. You're opposed to them on the surface, but what you're actually doing is cleaning up their messes.

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: When I saw you, I knew the rumors were true.

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: You were willing to go to jail for Rhine Lab.

options: Sounds right, but something feels off...

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Not the smartest thing to deal in rumors.

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: The fall of HydeBro was a headache for the Director of Energy, wasn't it?

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: The loss of a key supplier has thrown a wrench into his requests for a new laboratory site. He lost a few major orders, didn't he?

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: It was a setback to whatever experiments he had going on.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: It wasn't me who sent the Hyde brothers to jail.

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: You played a big part.

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: I know the rules. With the Hyde brothers locked up, the prosecutors no doubt wanted to use them to hook bigger fins.

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: Why was there no mention of Rhine Lab in the news? Why does Rhine always emerge unscathed from these things?

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: The truth is you've been following the trail, cleaning up all Rhine's little mistakes left along the way.

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: That's why you came looking for me...

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: You wanted to know whether or not Rhine had anything to do with this reagent.

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: Deep down, you're still the Rhine's Director of Defense. You still think it's your job to pick up after them.

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: There's something at Rhine that you can't let go of. Or maybe it's someone. Some sentiment.

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: Ha, looks like you do have emotions after all, Saria!

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: At the end of the day, we're all flesh and blood.

steps.name: Rhine Lab Tech
steps.text: The subject is out of control!

steps.name: Rhine Lab Tech
steps.text: Restraints have failed!

steps.name: Rhine Lab Tech
steps.text: Not getting any neural signals from the subject! Attempting sedative injection... negative!

steps.name: Rhine Defense Section Employee
steps.text: The subject is activating Originium Arts!

steps.name: Rhine Defense Section Employee
steps.text: A monster... it's a huge monster...

steps.name: Rhine Defense Section Employee
steps.text: No, the flames are manifesting...

steps.name: Rhine Defense Section Employee
steps.text: Get the Director on the line, now!

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Fire... the fire... cough...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Ifrit, where are you...?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Ifrit!

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Saria...?
She felt no heat in the fiery corridor.
The eyes of the Vouivre were harder than rock, colder than steel.
She could not read the emotions within them.
To this day, she does not know what she saw in the Vouivre's eyes.

steps.name: Sonny
steps.text: Are you okay, Doc Silence?

steps.name: Sonny
steps.text: You've gotta be tired.

steps.name: Sonny
steps.text: You've been taking care of Doc Moore, and the rest of us.

steps.name: Sonny
steps.text: I'm wicked sorry I acted like that, and almost got you hurt.

steps.name: Sonny
steps.text: Rhodes Island isn't like Rhine Lab. You and Greyy have been so good to us, and you never asked for nothing for it.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Is that true?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I'm no saint, Sonny.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I was a Rhine Lab researcher. My experiments almost wiped out an entire city block, countless people along with it...

steps.name: Sonny
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: There was a girl. She was close to me... almost like family.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: She was the subject of the experiment.

steps.name: Sonny
steps.text: What happened to her?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: She's still alive.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: But only alive. All these years, I've tried and failed to give her back the life she should have had, a normal life.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: But I couldn't stop the situation from deteriorating.

steps.name: Sonny
steps.text: Don't blame yourself. I'm sure you never meant to hurt her.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Ha... haha...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Funny, that's how I comforted myself in the past.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I didn't know. It was others who were truly to blame.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: But was that really so?
As the overseer in the field, did I really not know the risks of our research?
The answer is clear.
Either I was blinded by the tantalizing promise of a breakthrough...
Or I was far less a researcher than I thought I was.
And that's harder to do than to hate someone else.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Perhaps the one I truly could not forgive was...

steps.name: Sonny
steps.text: I never knew your story.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: It's more than just a story. It's why I came here.

steps.name: Sonny
steps.text: Aren't you trying to save your friend?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Of course, I have to save Joyce.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: But I want to save you, and Elena, and Director Franks.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I want to stop all this, before we get to the point of no return.

steps.name: Sonny
steps.text: You believe me?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Like I said, I believe in the truth, in what I see for myself.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: And I recall that I've seen something like it.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: The silver things following us—they look like the result of Originium Arts gone awry.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: By the way, I had Ben bring you something. It should be on your desk now.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Ben?

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: You forgot again? You told him to have tea with me. He talked so much that he nearly drank my entire stash.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: I don't remember you owing me anything.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Oh? That wasn't what you said when I'd just completed my chimeric organism experiments.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: The Diαbolic Experiments.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Glad you remember.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: My student used an anesthetic of her own design during the final phase.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: To shocking results.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Silence was such a smart girl. I miss her.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: After the project was suspended, I reviewed the data logs and found that it was no coincidence.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: What data?

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: You're not the only one who digs through the trash.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: You mean Loken Watertank? Those data were...

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Let's not dwell on clerical matters, shall we?

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Loken Williams was a genius. Reviewing his data made me realize that I was taking the long way round.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: I was trying to increase the subject's cell activity, in order to increase sync rate with the energy contained within the embedded shards.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Who would have thought that suppressing the subject's neural responses would be the way to go?

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Suppress?

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: I made some small changes to your formula based on this conjecture.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: I hope you'll forgive the initiative.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: You're a sly one, old goat.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Why the irritation? I simply offered a gift before you asked for it.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Is it really so disappointing to lose a weapon against me?

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: It had better be of use to my experiments.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: I promise you'll like it.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Oh, and if you're successful, could you pick up the tab on the ten boxes of black bean tea that Muelsyse owes me?

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: I would have won that bet, if not for my formula.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Back on topic.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: The reagent.

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: I had a sniff when you took it out.

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: Yes, it's the exact same smell.

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: Ha, it's the ghosts of the ones who died on my operating table, back to haunt me.

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: Thicker and more numerous...

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Who?

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: Who, you ask?

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: Who salvaged the most from the ruins of Loken Watertank?

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: Time to go home, Saria.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Rhine Lab.

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: See, you knew the answer all along.

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: You already met the Tin Man. He helped you find me.

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: Who was the main sponsor of the Diαbolic Experiments? Who was Loken Watertank's investor?

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: Who had the means to hire multiple labs to engage in similar experiments at the same time?

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: How irresistible did the order have to be, to make those labs put their petty patent feuds aside and sit down to share data?

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: And...

steps.name: Drunkard
steps.text: Whose hands did the surviving subjects pass through before they were sent out of Columbia?
Looks like a pretty lively conversation.
I hope I didn't miss too much.
